newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks recoup some losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks recoup some losses at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks slumped Wednesday as the market performed a downward correction, but pared losses at the close, dealers said.

"There was some strong selling in the most liquid stocks today before the market recovered a bit of ground. We expect this profit-taking to continue for while, but we don't see prices falling sharply," said trader Ignacio Lafuente at Banco Frances.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV fell 0.7 percent to 602.72, pulling off a session low of 597. It closed narrowly lower Tuesday and now stands level on the week.
"The market now has support at 590 points, and the outlook remains positive with a target of 620 before Christmas," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.

The MerVal has gained 5.7 percent so far this month and sentiment should be underpinned by private consultant FIEL's latest indicator Wednesday showing industrial production growth of 11.7 percent in October, traders said.

"However, we have to keep very close tabs on Wall Street, which seems unstoppable. It's a euphoric market which has virtually stayed firm for 12 running sessions, so we need to be extremely cautious," said Bonanno.
The broad market shed 0.6 percent, with losers outstripping winners 37 to 13 and 16 issues closing flat.
Floor volume eased to 22 million pesos from 23.1 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter deals picked up to 86.5 million pesos from 74.8 million Tuesday.

MerVal losers were led by textile firm Alpargatas and construction stock Polledo, off 3.3 percent and 3.1 percent, respectively. Best main-tier performers were power generator Capex and gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, up 2.2 percent and 1.6 percent, respectively.
